newsitem.title: UK: CE hopes no competition issues on N.Elec bid.
newsitem.headline: CE hopes no competition issues on N.Elec bid.

text.p: U.S. energy group CalEnergy is optimistic that there are no competition issues over its $1.225 billion bid for regional electricity company (Rec) Northern Electric, chairman David Sokol told Reuters.
"We are optimistic that the bid has nothing but pro-competitive aspects," he said in an interview.
Sokol said CalEnergy, which is making the bid through its 70 percent-owned unit CE Electric, had met with UK regulators to discuss the bid.
"We have met with all (relevant authorities) and attempted to respond to all their questions and enquiries," he said.
Electricity industry regulator Offer started its review of the bid on October 29 and said comments should be submitted by November 7.
Other UK authorities which would look at such a bid include the Office of Fair Trading and the Department of Trade and Industry.
CE Electric's bid at 630 pence per share has been clouded by market concerns it would not secure government approval and Northern shares have languished below the offer level.
At 1330 GMT, Northern was down three pence to 593-1/2 pence.
The government has already waved through seven takeovers of Recs, three from U.S. companies, leaving just five independent.
It blocked just two bids, from generators National Power and PowerGen, because these would have created integrated generators and distribution companies.
But current market concerns are that a looming general election might prompt the Conservative government, which lags in opinion polls, to refer the bid and avoid possible public criticism.
The electricity sector, privatised by the Conservatives in 1989, has reaped harsh comments from the press and opposition parties for hefty dividends, high executive pay and large takeover prices.
